item.title: Alex Floyd: A cut above: the story of Mary Beal
item.description: As America turns 250 and more attention is called to all levels of our history, it’s easy to focus on the “big people” and the turning point style events. item.title: Nutritional Wealth: When sugar is bittersweet
item.description: Not long ago, a major- league half-and-half sweet tea at a favorite Richmond Hill spot seemed like a harmless little “treat.” Cold, sweet, just the right amount of bite—pure Southern bliss in a glass. For a few minutes, it was perfect.

item.description: At this juncture of his letter, Paul begins to answer questions that have come to him from the church. Cases had arisen that went beyond Jewish instruction, and were not easily comprehended by the words of Christ, that needed the touch of an apostle to provide guidance.

item.title: A self-evaluation
item.description: In Psalm 109, verse 4, David describes himself as “a man of prayer”. I presume this means that he made prayer a regular habit; he had a consistent prayer life. David could have said several other positive things as well, such as having a servant’s heart and a desire to be holy, etc.

item.title: Americana Corner: The Battle of Tippecanoe
item.description: The last great battle between Indians in the old Northwest Territory and the forces of the United States, and one of the most consequential in our nation’s early decades, was the Battle of Tippecanoe, fought on November 7, 1811, between Shawnee, Potawatomi, and Kickapoo warriors and American troops led by General William Henry Harrison, the Governor of the Indiana Territory.

item.title: Wholesale Observations: St. Augustine, Florida
item.description: St. Augustine was founded by Spanish Admiral and conquistador Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, in 1565. The “Castillo de San Marco” (Castle of St. Mark) was built on the Matanzas river, beginning in 1672, to protect both the city and the state of Florida from various possible invaders. It is the oldest masonry fort in the continental United States, and today is a major tourist attraction. item.title: To meet labor demands, industries in Southeast Georgia turn to veterans
item.description: Southeast Georgia industries and economic leaders are tapping into “underutilized groups” to combat a predicted labor shortage, including a new focus on former military service members.

item.title: Soldier accused in August mass shooting changes plea
item.description: Sgt. Quornelius Radford was charged with two specifications of attempted premeditated murder and four specifications of attempted unpremeditated murder, among other charges, for an August 6 shooting incident in the 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team area on Fort Stewart.

item.title: Richmond Hill seeks another girls' soccer region title, playoff run
item.description: Senior defender Satori Bell and fellow defender sophomore Brooke Morgan are both assured that their team can bring home another region title and take a deeper step into the state playoffs.
